# 4 Maccabees Chapter 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** Historical Examples of Reason's Sovereignty

---

**1** Let me give you a few examples from Scripture to prove the point.

**2** One day during the war with the Philistines, David's men were exhausted and desperately thirsty toward evening. David himself longed intensely for water from a particular spring in enemy territory.

**3** Two of his bravest soldiers, wanting to please their king, strapped on their weapons, slipped past enemy lines, and drew water from the spring.

**4** When they brought it to David, he stopped and thought: if I drink this, it would be like drinking the blood of men who risked their lives to get it. So he refused to drink it and poured it out as an offering to God.

**5** Reason conquered desire.

**6** Now consider Joseph, that supremely self-disciplined man. When Potiphar's wife persistently threw herself at him, he refused again and again, because reason governed his desire.

**7** He was a young man with all the normal drives of youth, and yet he mastered his desire through reason.

**8** Reason is sovereign not just over sexual desire, but over every desire.

**9** The law itself says: do not covet your neighbor's wife or anything that belongs to your neighbor. Since the law commands us not to covet, I am all the more confident that reason can govern every passion.

**10** The same principle applies to all the passions that get in the way of justice. Just as a disciplined mind can overcome the drives of the body, so it can overcome the passions of the soul.

**11** Every person who truly lives by the whole law becomes master of their passions through reason. The law trains both the mind and the body.

**12** How can anyone who has seen all this refuse to believe that the mind is master of the passions?

**13** Even Moses, that great lawgiver, burned with anger when people turned against him, but he did not let that anger dictate his actions. He held it in check with reason.

**14** He stayed calm, went back to his duties, and when God appeared to him he responded with complete composure.

**15** That was the disciplined reason of Moses. He did not put out his anger — he channeled it through reason toward God's purposes.

**16** Reason does not kill the passions. It redirects them toward good and lawful goals.

**17** It turns anger away from murder and toward legitimate discipline; desire away from adultery and toward faithful love; greed away from theft and toward honest industry.

**18** By teaching the mind to be satisfied with what it truly needs, reason can master even the strongest craving.

**19** All the examples of self-denial performed by our ancestors in obedience to the law prove the same thing.

**20** Reason is truly sovereign over the passions.
